key_insight: AURORA-AI uses closed-loop control to dynamically reallocate compute across heterogeneous AI models so utility, fairness, robustness, and efficiency stay high under changing conditions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical orchestration strategy for deploying AI systems in real-world environments where drift, bias shocks, and sudden disruptions can degrade static resource policies.
method: Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman feedback control drives adaptive resource allocation.
Lyapunov-based monitoring enforces stability during operation.
A fairness-aware composite utility balances accuracy, demographic parity, latency, cost, robustness, and interpretability.
evidence_signal: In stress-rich discrete-time simulations with demographic bias shocks, concept drift, and black-swan disruptions, AURORA-AI outperformed Static, Round Robin, Greedy, LinUCB, and PPO on recovery speed and fairness/stability metrics.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate utility design and system modeling, so real deployments may face tuning overhead and sensitivity to mismatch between simulated and operational conditions.
paper_title: Adaptive Utility driven Resource Orchestration for Resilient AI (AURORA-AI)
